# CypherLite

> CypherLite is a lightweight, embeddable graph database written in Rust. It
> speaks Cypher — the most widely adopted graph query language — with
> zero infrastructure: no server, no configuration, no clusters. Think
> "SQLite for graphs".

## Why use it

- **Zero infrastructure**: an in-process embedded engine — open a path (or
  `:memory:`) and query. No server to run, ever.
- **Real Cypher**: 3891 of 3893 pinned openCypher TCK scenarios pass under a
  strict harness (the rest are documented skips), plus a large slice of
  Neo4j's post-standard Cypher 25 (GQL alignment) verified against a
  ~200-CIP evaluation suite: label expressions, quantified path patterns,
  path selectors, `SEARCH` (vector + full-text indexes), vector and UUID
  types, graph types, string interpolation, map comprehensions, `GROUP BY`,
  and more.
- **Durable by default**: an fsync'd local WAL with Parquet (or JSON)
  checkpoints — crash-safe single-file or directory databases.
- **Polyglot**: the public Rust crate (`cypherlite::Database`), a C ABI
  (FFI) wrapped by Python (DB-API + Arrow), JavaScript, Java, and Go
  clients, a CLI shell, and a Bolt server for remote access.
- **Fast + measurable**: in-memory graph with engine-owned indexes, frozen
  loadtest baselines as a merge gate.

## Install

```bash
curl -sSfL https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/install.sh | bash
```

Prebuilt binaries (incl. the `cypherlite-bolt` server) also live at
https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/dist/ and on the GitHub releases
page. Build from source with `cargo build --release`; the Python package is
`neo4j-cypherlite` (`import cypherlite`).

## Quick start

```bash
cypherlite                              # interactive shell, in-memory DB
cypherlite ./mygraph "RETURN 1 + 2"     # one-shot query
```

```cypher
CREATE (alice:Person {name: 'Alice', age: 30})
CREATE (bob:Person {name: 'Bob', age: 28})
CREATE (alice)-[:FRIENDS_WITH {since: 2020}]->(bob)
MATCH (p:Person)-[r:FRIENDS_WITH]->(friend)
RETURN p.name, friend.name, r.since;
```

Python:

```python
import cypherlite
db = cypherlite.connect(":memory:")
db.execute("CREATE (p:Person {name: $name})", {"name": "Alice"})
for row in db.execute("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name"):
    print(row["p.name"])
```

## Use it with AI agents

The CLI ships an agent skill: `cypherlite skill install` (with `--agent
claude-code|cursor|windsurf|copilot|...`) installs a skill bundle that
teaches the agent CypherLite's CLI, Cypher dialect, and data model, so
agents can drive a local graph database without a server.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/getting-started):
  install and your first queries in under 5 minutes
- [Tutorials](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/category/tutorial):
  first graph, social network, vector search, Python
- [Guides](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/category/guides):
  vector similarity (incl. `SEARCH` and hybrid), geospatial, CSV import,
  backup/restore, output formats
- [Cypher syntax reference](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/reference/cypher-syntax):
  every supported clause and expression
- [Functions reference](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/reference/functions)
- [CLI reference](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/reference/cli):
  flags, dot-commands, `skill`/`upgrade` lifecycle commands
- [Rust API](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/reference/rust) ·
  [Python library](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/reference/python) ·
  [C API](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/reference/c) ·
  [Bolt](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/reference/bolt)
- [TCK compliance](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/reference/tck):
  the openCypher conformance claim, methodology, and skip list
- [Architecture](https://neo4j-labs.github.io/cypherlite/docs/explanation/architecture):
  how the engine works (WAL, checkpoints, planner, executor)

## Scope notes

Single-process and single-user by design: no RBAC/users/roles, clustering,
or multi-database administration (that Cypher surface is intentionally out
of scope — see the per-CIP scope decisions in the repository's
`testdata/cip-eval/MANIFEST.md`). Remote access is via the bundled Bolt
server; language clients wrap the C ABI.

Source: https://github.com/neo4j-labs/cypherlite — Apache-2.0.
